name: isolated Git branch as bounded atomic text/binary publication substrate
objective: Replace several richer-mode outcomes at once—durable file state, actual small binary persistence, atomic multi-file publication, optimistic conflict rejection, readback and idempotent retry—using scheduled Chat repository APIs only.

mechanism.content_layer: Git blobs are content-addressed; current connector accepts utf-8 or base64, so text and non-UTF8 bytes can both be stored.
mechanism.snapshot_layer: A Git tree names the complete file set. Multiple role-local blob entries can be added to one tree before publication.
mechanism.transaction_layer: A commit binds the tree to one fresh parent. A single force=false branch-ref update makes the whole committed tree the branch-visible state.
mechanism.conflict_layer: If another sibling commit advances the branch, force=false rejects the stale sibling as non-fast-forward. Recovery fresh-reads the new head and recomputes a descendant commit instead of forcing the stale candidate.
mechanism.retry_layer: Stable branch/path/op identities are queried first; expected existing blob/tree state => DONE_NOOP. Recreating identical blobs is content-idempotent.
mechanism.authority_layer: Use a unique unprotected role-local evidence branch. Do not update protected/primary authority as part of this substrate.

live_evidence.interpretation: Both previously absent files became branch-visible only after the single ref publication; the ref points to one commit/tree containing both.

transversal_outcomes.duplicate_retry: SUPPORTED by query/reconcile plus content identity

quota_and_cost.ordinary_repository_limits: Protocol remains low-volume and deliberately bounded below GitHub's recommended ordinary-object limits.

scope_limits: Atomicity is branch-ref visibility of one Git tree, not a general database transaction.
force=false is non-fast-forward protection, not explicit expected-old-SHA CAS; unique role branches and fresh reconstruction are required.
Persistent repository branches/objects consume ordinary repository size, so the mechanism is bounded and not a bulk binary store.
No claim is made that external systems can execute or ingest the stored bytes without their own exposed connector/API.
